analysis: The trial completed successfully but reached macro validation HR@10 of 0.4713, below the referenced 0.5537 by 0.0824. Category HR@10 was 0.505 for Movies_and_TV, 0.525 for Industrial_and_Scientific, 0.345 for Electronics, and 0.510 for CDs_and_Vinyl. Electronics was the weakest category. These results do not support candidate-conditioned attention as an improvement in this configuration. Randomly hiding any historical purchase may misalign training with next-purchase prediction, while separate embeddings and learned attention may need stronger regularization or more supervision. These are hypotheses; the reported metrics do not isolate the cause.
code_summary: Trains a separate attentive item-similarity model for each of four categories. Separate history and candidate embeddings produce pairwise scores, weighted by candidate-conditioned attention with square-root normalization. Training hides one purchased item, drops some context items, and applies cross-entropy against 16 unseen negatives using AdamW. Checkpoints are selected by validation HR@10, with NDCG@10 breaking ties. The predictor writer loads the matching architecture and checkpoints, preserves dataset routing, and scores candidates against the latest 128 history items.
